Task 1. You will listen to a meeting at Aberdeen College where people are discussing the college’s new online systems.

OK, good morning, everybody.
Thanks for coming to the meeting today.
I know today’s Saturday and I'm sure you've got other things to do on a Saturday morning, but hopefully the meeting will be a short one.
Do you two.
know each other?
No, I don’t think so.
OK, well, this is Rob Lee.
Rob’s the College Technician, so he can advise us on technical and Rob Hi.
Hi. Yeah, and Rob I think you know Cherry.
Our Student President?
OK. Right so, as I said in my email, I wanted to discuss what needs to be done to improve the College’s online systems.
So maybe we could start with the college website.
Any comments from students about the website?
Well, the first thing I've written here about the website is that it’s like boring.
Students are always saying that Yeah, I agree with Cherry actually.
It’s a bit boring.
I think the thing that I would add would be that it’s not user friendly.
Yeah, I'd agree.
It certainly isn’t user -friendly.
What about the other services, like the Intranet system for teachers.
Intranet? Is that, like, where the teachers can communicate with each other?
Yeah, the teachers can use the intranet to send files as well like documents, pictures, video clips.
Well, Why don’t they just use their email?
Because it isn't secure.
You know it's it’s not safe to send files like that.
And the internet has the advantage that it’s secure because it’s protected by the College’s firewall.
Hmm, OK, let’s move on.
What kinds of things would we like to see available online line from the new system?
Cherry? Well, I think a social network.
You know, something like Facebook.
Maybe a place where we could chat online about school stuff with schoolmates and teachers Wait so you would want teachers to be able to go to this social network as well?
As well as students I mean.
Sure, why not?
OK, well that’s one idea.
What else? How about an online market?
What, like, for people to buy and sell things?
Yeah, a market.
I was thinking you know, we could like sell things like our old textbooks books and students in lower forms could buy them.
Sounds good. I think that would work.
Right, OK. Let’s move on to the action we need to take, First, the website, can you be responsible for that Rob?
For what? The re-design of the website Well, my programming I mean, they're pretty basic.
But I know a web designer so I could contact him.
Maybe. to give us a price Okay, Right, So you contact the web designer then Rob.
How about the other systems we talked about?
Well. why don’t I carry out a survey of the students to see what it is they want from our online systems?
Great idea, Cherry.
It’s really important that we get the students views on this.
I think a survey of the students is an excellent idea.
So yeah, you can do that Cherry.
Fine And I'll do the same with the teachers.
We need to get their input as well.
So a survey is good.
Right. OK, so that’s about all we can do today.
Let's meet again next week at the same time.
I’m sorry, I think I'll need more time than a week.
Can we meet in two week’s time?
OK, two weeks it is then.
That is the end of Task 1.

a page for Parents, so that they can get information about the College from their perspective.

a College wins cup?

Right, the next one.

Hmm. OK. And that’s about it for the home page.
Good. Have you had time to work on any of the other pages?
Yeah, OK. we've been working on the Students page.
Just a second.
So here it is.
The Students Page.
There will be all the same things at the top of the page as on the home page, so I haven't included them on the demo.

will be of interest to the students.
So we have Transport at the top of the list Good.
If the students can’t get here then you can’t teach them very much can you?
That's what I always say!

that we have introduced.
It’s still in production so we can’t show it to you yet, but users will be able to access it from here.

That last one build relationships it'd be really good if we could use the website to build relationships, you know between students students and students and between students and teachers.
Yeah. So, the other major thing we've included on the menu On the Students page is Akadeem.
the new learning management system.
Eko, what? Akadeem, A -C -A -D -E -M -E.
it means the academic or learning environment And also begins with AC, for Aberdeen College!

We can provide the information here.

I -C -A -R -U -S Icarus Liu How are you?

to learn much more than we do.

creative software you know to draw or design things Oh, right.

Do you think it would be a good idea?

I just think it’s dangerous, Dangerous?
Dangerous how Grace?

I mean if you do post your phone number, it’s really stupid.
Yeah, but you can control who sees your information.
I know. I know you can But a lot of students just don’t bother and they say yes to every friend request, even if they don’t know that person.

I would never give out personal information like my home address or whatever.
But often people do.
That's the point.
I think some students are just too eager to make new friends No, the point is that people need to learn that doing that sort of thing is stupid Michael?

Making friends online is one of the great benefits of having an online social network.
network. It’s part of the reality of the outside world.

you want to listen to that podcast I was telling you about?

The idea of email becoming extinct anytime soon may seem silly.
But chances are strong that you used web -based email less in 2011 than in 2010.
A recent report, The 2012 U .S.
Digital Year in Review, showed that web -based email usage was down for just about every age group under 55 from 2010 to 2011, with the 12 to 17 age group showing the largest
just decline at a staggering 59 Web -based email or webmail refers to email access through a browser.
so think Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo!
mail, et cetera, as the majority of email usage analyzed in this report.
This means that the groups of people who make up the majority of internet users and have the most experienced with email are now actually moving away from the medium.
The report also noted that email usage among seniors has increased, which isn’t surprising as a larger percentage of older people today have had more exposure to the web than their predecessors.
The report also went into detail on what sites people spent their time on.
It showed time spent on webmail sites declined while social networking sites has shown a drastic increase.
People are spending more time on social networking sites and less time on email sites and this is good news for social network sites.
Last fall Facebook founder, Mark Zuckerberg predicted the death of email when he introduced Facebook's new messaging interface, face.
We don’t think that a modern messaging system is going to be email, Zuckerberg said at a press conference in San Francisco.
Facebook users are now able to communicate through Facebook via text, email or instant message and receive communications from all of these avenues through one news feed.
Users typically value when related information from a variety of channels is consolidated into one place and that’s what Facebook’s messaging interface is trying to accomplish for users.
Many organisations with well -established IT departments have typically hosted email in -house, whereas others as of lately have turned to cloud email services services like Gmail.
This switch is attractive as it simply cuts costs.
While many companies and large universities are making the switch to cloud -based email services, will they make another shift towards using social networks to communicate?

One social networking system that businesses are turning to is called Collabro Chatter, a business collaboration tool which which describes itself as an effective means of connecting with prospective customers.

efficiency. efficiency. And increased productivity and efficiency is music to any boss’s ears in these or any times Well that’s it.

I'm Aline Lee.
Welcome to this week's Bookmark and we are delighted to have Lionel Chen as our special guest today.
Welcome Lionel. Thank you, it’s great to be here.
We are going to talk about your new book today, but before we do that, I know you'd like to mention an important community event that’s happening soon OK, yeah, it’s a Fun Day.

There'll be lots of people from different countries there OK.
so, if we want to come along we need to get down to Kaloon Park on the 15th of April.

Right. So what will be happening in the Fun Day?
Okay? There'll be lots of activities like a lucky draw.

Yeah, but don’t just come for the lucky draw.
I think the Fun day is actually very important.
It’s a great chance for people from different cultures to meet each other.
So a lucky draw and a chance to meet people from different cultures.
Sounds good. And will you be there?
Yeah, I'll be there, yeah.
There, Another one of the activities at the Fun Day is I'm giving a talk about body language.
A talk about body language?
Is there much to say about body language then?
Well, yeah. Yes, there is.
We communicate using our bodies and it’s something we really should be more aware of.
OK, like what for example?
Well, the classic example is eye contact.
Eye contact is the aspect of non -verbal communication that varies most from country to country.
Really? Yes, for example the length of time that people’s eyes meet.
If your eyes meet with someone for a long time it can mean at least three different things depending on the country.
Three different things?
Yeah? For example, in some countries it means you want to fight So too much eye contact can mean a sort of challenge, is that it?
Well, yes, But in other countries it can mean something totally different.
It can also mean that you are showing that you are really interested in what the person is saying.
Right. And the third?
Yes, well, the third possible meaning of a long meeting of the eyes is, of course, romantic That you're interested in that person romantically.
Well, there's a bit of a difference there then!
You want to fight, you're interested or you want to be his girlfriend!
Exactly. And can you give me some advice to people about eye contact then?
Well, I think the best advice is to try to become aware of what you do yourself and adapt to the situation Sounds like good advice.
become aware of what I do with my eyes and adapt to the situation I’m in!
Yes, that’s it!
Now, I know.
we know that you'll be giving a talk at the Fun Day, but some of our listeners might not know that much about you.

No. No. Singapore.
OK, my mistake.

Oh for about 10 years I suppose.

I’m always interested to read what you have to say about communication barriers and how they affect us.
I'm interested to know, what about those barriers that are particular to Hong Kong or barriers that are a real problem in Hong Kong compared to other places?

Yeah, I can imagine that.
Noise, time and people not listening sounds like Hong Kong on a bad day!
Well, yes. It might be quite amusing but these are all genuine barriers to communication in Hong Kong.

A barrier stops something from happening.
Hmm, Ok, so a barrier stops something from happening.
Right And the important thing is what happens next.
As I say, a barrier like noise stops communication happening.
but it’s how that affects people, that’s the point.
Tick noise as an example.
We all know Hong Kong can be very noisy But what happens when it’s so so noisy that we just can’t communicate?
I know I just get angry.
Well, you're not alone Arlene.

OK, I'll have to look for a quiet space to talk then!
You mentioned newcomers arriving in Hong Kong.
You mean people from outside China.
Yes, well the people I meet in Hong Kong are from everywhere.
From Africa, from South America, from the Middle East.
These people come to Hong Kong to start new lives.
Just like I did.
Some people need help to deal with the practical difficulties.
What kinds of difficulties do they need help with?
Well, things like finding schools for their children.
There are two difficulties here.
firstly to find a school, and secondly, to fill in the school application form, Some newcomers don’t really have the written skills in English or Chinese to fill in those long government forms.
Yeah, well, I find filling in those forms bad enough.
love. But if it’s something as important as finding a school for their children, then that sounds like something really worthwhile to do.
OK. Oh, before I forget, we need to give our listeners some information about your new book.

It’s available in all major bookstores in Hong Kong.
All big of course at the Fun Day at Kaloon Park on April 15th.
Oh yes, of course at the Fun Day as well, Well, I'd recommend all our listeners to give it a try It really is a good read.
Well Lionel, it’s been very nice to meet you and thanks for coming into the port today.
